subject: Unexpected mid-cycle ingestion charges from staging traffic
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <ap@brightlane.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle ingestion charges from staging traffic

Hi Jonas,

We're seeing a ~$1.1k charge on invoice INV-1679 that looks like it came from what our engineers believe was staging traffic. This was mid-cycle and unexpected — we run an automated stress test in staging weekly and it should be billed to a sandbox project, not production.

Can you please:
- Hold collection on this invoice while we investigate (AP will not remit until clarified)
- Share a per-request usage export (raw logs) and the attribution keys used so we can map tokens back to our internal runs
- Let us know if Redwood can issue a provisional credit if this proves to be staging traffic accidentally billed to prod

I attached INV-1679.

Thanks,
Emily Zhang
Director of Finance | BrightLane
accounts-payable@brightlane.ai

Attachment: INV-1679.pdf (invoice, 1 page)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.inference
To: Emily Zhang <ap@brightlane.ai>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.inference, ben.carter@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-08-14T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle ingestion charges from staging traffic

Hi Emily — thanks for flagging this. I've looped in Marcus (CS lead) and Ben (billing) to investigate.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- We'll pull a per-request export for the window on 2026-08-12 00:00 UTC to 2026-08-13 23:59 UTC and share a snapshot today. (provisional file: preliminary-usage-snapshot.csv)
- Can you confirm the sandbox/project tenant IDs your engineering team used during the test? That will help us map attribution rules.
- We'll pause automated collection and mark INV-1679 as "under review" in our billing system to prevent auto-pay.

If this is caused by customer-side mis-tagging (staging using a prod API key), we will propose a provisional credit while we complete the audit.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference

Attachment: preliminary-usage-snapshot.csv (CSV, 1MB)

From: ben.carter@redwood.inference
To: jonas.weber@redwood.inference
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.inference, Emily Zhang <ap@brightlane.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle ingestion charges from staging traffic

Short summary of our audit so far:
- We exported token/endpoint attribution for the UTC window requested and sampled the request IDs.
- ~42,178 tokens were flagged under project id 'prod-nyc-82' between 2026-08-12 02:03 and 2026-08-12 02:26 UTC.
- Sampled request headers show the same API key and no staging label present in the request metadata. However, comment field in a subset of requests includes "staging-run-08" which suggests the client app was running a staging workload while authenticating with the prod key.

Provisional remediation:
- We can issue a provisional credit of $1,120 (calculated at your plan rate) contingent on a final audit and confirmation from your engineering team.
- We'll provide a full request log export (redacted PII) to your engineers for mapping. Link: https://drive.redwood.inference/shared/brightlane/usage-export-20260814.csv

Next steps we need from BrightLane:
- Confirm the tenant/project IDs used in the test and any API keys rotated during that window.
- Confirm you want the provisional credit applied immediately or after the final audit.

Attachment: token-sample-logs.gz (gzip, 200KB)

From: Emily Zhang <ap@brightlane.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.inference
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.inference, marcus.lin@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-08-15T13:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle ingestion charges from staging traffic

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Ben.

We ran a forced load in staging during that slot and our infra lead confirms a scripting error pointed the staging run at the org-level API key (prod) rather than the sandbox key. That would explain the presence of "staging-run-08" in the comment field while attribution shows the prod project id.

Please apply the provisional credit of $1,120 immediately and issue an updated invoice/credit memo we can attach to our AP system. We will rotate the keys and share the sandbox tenant IDs for future reference.

Can you also confirm: will Redwood add a label-based attribution safeguard so that requests containing a recognized "staging" tag are excluded from billing if they originate from a sandbox project in the future? That would prevent repeats.

Emily Zhang
Director of Finance | BrightLane
accounts-payable@brightlane.ai

Attachment: none

From: jonas.weber@redwood.inference
To: Emily Zhang <ap@brightlane.ai>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.inference, ben.carter@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-08-16T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle ingestion charges from staging traffic

Emily — thanks, and appreciate the confirmation from your infra team.

Action items completed / timeline:
- Ben has approved a provisional credit of $1,120 which will be reflected as a credit memo against INV-1679. You'll receive the formal credit memo and an updated invoice within 3 business days. (Attachment to follow: credit-proposal-draft.pdf)
- Collections: we've flagged the invoice as on-hold in our receivables system so AP will not be prompted to collect. Please do not remit until you receive the updated invoice and credit memo.
- Root cause: client-side misconfiguration (staging run using org-level API key).
- Mitigations we will implement: 1) provide the per-request export link (shared above) for your engineers to map requests, 2) add an optional label-based filter in billing that customers can enable to exclude requests that include a recognized staging/sandbox header (we'll scope this as an account-level toggle; ETA: Q4 2026), 3) recommend immediate API key rotation for the affected org key.

If you want, Marcus can run a short post-mortem call with your infra lead to walk through the logs next week.

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference

Attachment: credit-proposal-draft.pdf (PDF, 1 page)
